thread:
ops-bot: NIGHTDASH alert: 03:12 UTC - p50 latency +45% and tail spikes on the runtime cohort (canary). https://grafana.redwood/d/overview/nightdash?panelId=7 :rotating_light:

alice: seeing the same on the canary host pool, mid-merge window. Noticing a bunch of kernel-switch events in the logs.

sam: can you paste the alert graph? I only have the slack summary.

alice: pasted — p50 jump lines up around 03:06 right after merge of CL #4821 (kernel-selector heuristics).

irene: hmm, #4821 changed the selector epsilon and batching window favoring low-latency kernels for short sequences. Could be interacting with KV cache churn.

luis: CI perf also failed on nightly perf-run 2024-06-03 03:00 (job perf-runtime-vec). Failure: 7% regress p95 across microbenchmarks. Link: https://ci.redwood/builds/perm/7421

alice: logs from canary:
```
[03:06:41] kernel_selector: selected kernel=fast_attn_v2 for model=redwood-small seq_len=64
[03:06:41] kv_cache: evict candidate=hotset-entry-0x7f3 size=1.2MB
[03:06:42] batching: window_ms flipped from 8 -> 2
[03:06:42] cpu/jitter: user 78% -> 94%
```

sam: batching window flip to 2ms looks wrong during a merge. That should be 8ms steady for this traffic pattern. Which commit changed default window?

irene: #4821 touched selector and also added dynamic-window heuristic. It falls back by threshold if memory pressure or kernel mismatch but threshold calc uses stale hotset sizes. Could be miscalc.

luis: I ran a quick profile on a repro VM: increased syscalls from cache eviction, and fast_attn_v2 has higher memcpy for short kv slices. When combined with small batch window we get more kernel handoffs and higher latency.

alice: OK, can we revert the dynamic-window part in #4821 to unblock rollout? We need to stop tail from oscillating overnight.

sam: opened PR to revert dynamic-window heuristic: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4860 (revert part only). Can we hotfix in canary first?

irene: suggest bisect to confirm root cause before revert. Start with merge base at v1.18.0 -> HEAD. I'll run git bisect locally and check nightly perf script.

luis: meanwhile, adding a quick runtime guard to disable selector epsilon if kv_evictions > 10/min on node. Low-risk toggle. I can push as a flags-only change.

alice: good plan. If the guard reduces kernel switches we can keep canary while bisect runs.

ci-bot: CI job perf-runtime-vec re-run queued by sam (PR 4860).

ops-bot: deploy: canary pool updated with flag 'selector.dynamic_window=false' on 03:34 UTC by ops. Rolling 10% -> 50% -> 100% if stable.

alice: post-flag: tail latency back down within 12min, p95 recovered to baseline. Thanks luis.

irene: bisect results: culprit narrowed to commit 7f1ad3c (part of #4821) — dynamic-window threshold calc uses heap snapshot that can be stale under concurrent eviction. I'll propose a fix that recalculates on latch and adds tests.

sam: do we want to merge fix or revert? Revert PR is ready if we hit more regressions overnight.

luis: fix LGTM but higher-risk than revert. If we ship fix include guard anyway as defense.

alice: decision: revert dynamic-window in prod to be safe, merge fix to main with tests, then reintroduce behind gate. I'll approve PR 4860 revert and keep guard.

sam: I'll monitor nightdash and set alert thresholds tighter for kernel-switch delta.

alice: thanks everyone — great triage. Follow-up: please add a short postmortem note to the release checklist and link perf graphs + bisect PR. :thumbsup:
